title: Controlled Multi-Agent Orchestration Preparation Foundation
goal: Prepare explicit role, provenance, and orchestration primitives before any multi-agent runtime is activated.
scope: Translate the documented multi-agent red-team direction into inactive control-plane primitives such as role definitions, allowed handoff types, provenance metadata, policy checks, and operator-visible activation requirements. Do not enable distributed AI runtime behavior, hidden agents, autonomous tool use, or uncontrolled worker coordination.
generation_reason: AI_PENTESTING_AGENT.md and docs/multi_agent_red_team_program.md both point to a future controlled multi-agent layer that needs explicit preparation before activation.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Preparation only. Do not activate multiple AI agents, hidden workflows, distributed offensive behavior, or uncontrolled worker lanes.

success_criteria: Agent roles, handoff boundaries, policy checks, and provenance metadata are represented as inactive planning primitives.
Activation requirements are visible and stricter than normal single-agent planning.
No multi-agent runtime behavior or hidden orchestration is enabled.
Worker identity and evidence provenance requirements are documented before implementation.
Tests cover inactive defaults, forbidden activation, and provenance metadata shape where code is added.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Multi-agent primitives remain inactive by default.
No hidden distributed offensive runtime is introduced.
Activation requirements preserve scope, provenance, approval, and kill-switch controls.

before_promotion: Assessment pattern library and pack effectiveness foundation is completed and logged.
Role, handoff, policy, and provenance boundaries are documented.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with multi-agent preparation changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with inactive multi-agent preparation status and activation limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
